summary: Joseph Hackin was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Sylvain Lévi, Louis Finot, Édouard Chavannes, and Paul Pelliot, later directing the Maison Franco-Japonaise and the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan.

Joseph Haekel earned his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna between 1931 and 1935. He spent his career there as Wilhelm Koppers's assistant, Privatdozent from 1941, and ordinary professor and director beginning in 1957.

Joseph Haroutunian worked in religious studies and philosophy. After studying at the American University of Beirut, Columbia University, and Union Theological Seminary, he held posts at Wellesley College, McCormick Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago.

Joseph Light Wyatt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St Augustine's College, Canterbury, and Christ's College, Cambridge. In 1895, he served as a university teacher at the University of Cambridge.

Joseph Loizzo specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College, Harvard University, and under Robert A. F. Thurman and Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche, and served as a visiting scholar of religion at Columbia University.

Joseph M. Kitagawa was a religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. under Joachim Wach at the University of Chicago. He taught at Chicago from 1951, later serving as Dean of the Divinity School.

Joseph Mansion was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Ghent University and studied under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He joined the University of Liège as chargé de cours in 1904, becoming extraordinary professor in 1910.
Joseph Margolis was a philosopher who completed an M.A. at Columbia University between 1948 and 1950. He held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University in 1991.

Joseph A. Marino is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed degrees at Ohio State University and the University of Washington, where he studied under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox and became an assistant professor in 2020.

Joseph Masson was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned a doctorate at KU Leuven. He taught at the Institut Saint-Robert Bellarmin, the University of Namur, and served as professor at the Pontifical Gregorian University from 1958.
Joseph Menrad was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Munich between 1883 and 1888. He served as school director at Willibald-Gymnasium from 1921 to 1926.

Joseph Merkel was an Indologist who taught at Karls-Universität Aschaffenburg from 1810. He served as a professor at the Gymnasium Aschaffenburg from 1818 and became court librarian at Hofbibliothek Aschaffenburg in 1828.

Joseph Mullens was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Coward College, the University of London, Williams College, and the University of Edinburgh. He served as foreign secretary for the London Missionary Society from 1865.

Joseph Nadin Rawson worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Jesus College, Oxford, under Arthur Anthony Macdonell and J. N. Farquhar, and served as professor of religion at Serampore College from roughly 1913 to 1937.

Joseph Needham was a Sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Cambridge. He served as a fellow of Gonville and Caius College, reader in biochemistry at Cambridge, and director of the Needham Research Institute from roughly 1976 to 1990.
Joseph Peet was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington, in 1829. He later served as principal of CMS College Kottayam from roughly 1835 to 1838.

Joseph Prabhu is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied under Bernard Williams, John N. Findlay, and Alasdair MacIntyre. He held an associate professorship of philosophy at California State University, Los Angeles.

Joseph Ratzinger was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Munich and the Ducal Georgianum. He held academic posts at the universities of Bonn, Münster, Tübingen, Regensburg, and Munich between 1959 and 1982.

Joseph Rock was a Sinologist and Tibetologist. He held positions at Mills College, the Mid-Pacific Institute, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, the United States Department of Agriculture, the Army Map Service, and the Harvard-Yenching Institute.
Joseph Rupp was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich between 1841 and 1845. He served as a gymnasium professor at Dom-Gymnasium Freising from 1850 to 1882.
